title: Support trace primer and replay snippets
body:
Purpose
This is a compact, practical primer for support engineers and oncall responders to quickly find, interpret and (when feasible) replay or synthesize traces for inference requests. The intent: reduce time-to-insight for customer-impacting latency/quality incidents without requiring deep familiarity with the full tracer schema.

Scope and audience
- Primary: support engineers, SREs on first-line triage.
- Secondary: product and devs that own inference routes.
- Not a formal instrumentation spec — that lives in trace-standards Confluence. This is a hands-on cheat-sheet + example queries + replay snippets.

High-level approach (three quick steps)
1) Narrow by user/request context: customer_id, route, request_id, or time-window. Prefer request_id if present.
2) Skim summary spans: route-router, model-select, kv-cache-lookup, runtime-infer, token-stream, response-serialize. Look for long durations or error tags.
3) If root cause unclear, extract minimal span set (request_id, model-instance-id, node-host, quantization-profile) and run preorder checks: CPU/GPU util, host OOM, burst tokens, batching event.

Common span names to look for (quick reference)
- req.receive
- http.router (edge LB)
- route.resolve
- model.lookup
- kv.cache.get
- batch.queue.wait
- batch.dispatch
- runtime.infer
- tokenizer.encode / tokenizer.decode
- stream.write
- response.serialize

Search examples (use service logs/traces UI)
- By request id: trace.request_id:abc123 -> single-trace view.
- Last 15 minutes for high token latency: http.router AND runtime.infer.latency>200ms AND env:prod
- Find dropped traces (sampling gap): service:runtime AND !trace_id -> then cross-correlate with request logs using request_id if available.

Quick grep/snippet examples for local trace dump (if you have a raw ndjson of spans)
- find root spans: jq 'select(.parent_id==null) | {trace_id, span_name, duration_ms}' span_dump.ndjson
- top offenders by duration: jq '(.duration_ms as $d | {trace_id, span: .name, d: $d})' span_dump.ndjson | sort -r -k3 | head -n 20

Minimal investigative checklist (first 10 min)
- Confirm scope: single-tenant vs multi-tenant impact.
- Request-level: request_id, route, model, model_version, quantization flag.
- Resource-level: host/gpu id, mem/cpu/gpu metrics at timestamp.
- Telemetry: check for corresponding error logs or OOM events.
- Trace-level: was the long duration in kv cache, batching, or model runtime?
- If batching: did batch size spike? Was queue wait time abnormally high?

When to synthesize a replay trace
- Use replay when you need to reproduce latency profile and you have: the original prompt (or redacted prompt), request metadata, and a non-sensitive small test input. Replays are only allowed on anonymized inputs unless permitted by customer policy.

Replay recipe (low-cost synthetic)
1) Recreate request metadata: route, model_version, quantized:true/false, session/context length.
2) Use a single small input that approximates token length distribution. For stateful sessions, include previous prompt markers but redact PII.
3) Run against a warmed instance (same model_variant if available) with controlled concurrency = 1.
4) Collect spans + host metrics and compare duration distribution vs original trace.

Example: replay command for local dev harness (pseudo)
- ./replay_harness --model redwood-3b-int8 --route "chat" --input "[redacted]" --session-len 512 --concurrency 1 --collect-spans > out.ndjson

Span enrichment rules we rely on (what support expects to see)
- span.tags must include: request_id, customer_id (hashed), model_variant, host_id, gpu_id (if available), batch_id (if used), quantization_profile.
- Errors should carry human-readable short_error and canonical_error_code.

Dashboard quick-sketches (operator view)
1) Topline: 95th/99th runtime.infer latency, median batch.queue.wait, token throughput per-host. Time window: 15m/1h/24h toggles.
2) Heatmap: per-route latency quantiles by hour (rows=routes, cols=hour) to spot skew.
3) Incident detail panel: selected request_id -> span waterfall + host metrics + last 100 logs.
4) Cost/latency tradeoff widget: batch_size vs p50/p95 tokens/sec for recent 24h; annotate recent rollout changes.

Privacy guardrails (quick reminders)
- Never paste raw customer prompts into public Slack or tickets. Use redacted placeholders.
- Replays against production data require approval from privacy on a per-customer basis.

Short list of actionable improvements (notes to engineering)
- Add batch_id to spans emitted by batcher (currently sometimes missing).
- Emit quantization_profile as a top-level tag on root span.
- Add a compact error_reason tag for quick triage (e.g., kv-miss, oom, auth-fail, tokenization-error).
- Provide a canned query in the traces UI for "top runtime.infer outliers last 1h".

Unresolved questions / follow-ups
- Sampling: how often do we capture full-tokenized spans for long-running requests? Current sample rate unclear (need a telemetry owner).
- Cross-tenant noise: how to better filter host-level noise when diagnosing single-tenant slowdowns on shared pools?
- Replays: can we maintain a small, privacy-safe corpus for synthetic replays that approximates worst-case token shapes?

Quick references and bookmarks
- Trace naming/convention (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/trace-standards
- Jira for batch improvements: INF-3421
- Dev PR for span tags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287

Notes to oncall: keep this doc open during triage. If you hit missing span tags, create INF ticket and include trace_id + small sample of spans (redacted). For any PII suspicion escalate to Privacy.

Notes to authors: This is intentionally terse — convert any recurring checklist items into shareable queries or a one-click dashboard in the traces UI.

Revision history
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (Asha)
- 2025-02-25: added replay recipe + grep snippets (Maya)
- 2025-03-02: clarified span tags and added unresolved questions (Jon)
